decisions.rationale: Lead Rotom-Wash + Spiritomb. Rotom OHKOs Gyarados, survives physical hits, and pressures Corviknight/Mamoswine; Spiritomb safely checks Gengar, can Taunt/burn, and takes Gengar hits. Talonflame is back for Tailwind, Quick Guard against Ice Shard/Sucker Punch, and late cleaning, but must avoid Rock Slide/Waterfall. Garchomp provides Life Orb Earthquake insurance vs Gengar and Rock Slide vs Gyarados. Bench Aegislash/Floette.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Gengar-Mega (Timid, Shadow Tag), Corviknight (Tailwind/U-turn), Mamoswine (Focus Sash, Ice Shard/EQ/Rock Slide), Gyarados (Intimidate, Waterfall/Crunch/Taunt); all Protect. Benched Klefki/Toxapex. Key calcs: Rotom Thunderbolt OHKOs Gyarados through Sitrus; Hydro Pump forces Mamoswine Sash; Rotom takes Corviknight Brave Bird, Gyarados Waterfall, Mamoswine Rock Slide/Ice Shard well. Spiritomb checks Gengar: Sucker Punch 2x, survives Shadow Ball/Sludge Bomb; Taunt/burn are central. Mamoswine Rock Slide OHKOs Talonflame even as spread; Gyarados Waterfall OHKOs Talonflame; Ice Shard can OHKO Garchomp. Garchomp EQ nearly OHKoes Mega Gengar and can threaten Gyarados with Rock Slide if Rotom is compromised. Talonflame provides Tailwind/Quick Guard and priority, but should not switch into Rock Slide/Waterfall or Gengar Thunderbolt. Plan: lead Rotom-Wash + Spiritomb; back Talonflame + Garchomp. Keep Rotom healthy as Gyarados answer. Use Spiritomb Taunt to deny Protect/status, burn physical attackers. If they bring Klefki, avoid Spiritomb Play Rough and use Fire/Ground/Steel answers; if Toxapex, Taunt and Rotom/Garchomp pressure. Bench Aegislash/Floette unless needing extra Wide Guard or Fairy/Psychic emergency.

decisions.rationale: Lead Gengar-Mega+Gyarados per plan: Intimidate+Shadow Tag to trap and eliminate Rotom-W/Spiritomb early. Mamoswine back for Ice Shard priority on Talonflame/Garchomp, kept clean via Focus Sash. Toxapex back for Haze vs Calm Mind Floette and Toxic attrition into their stall. Corviknight excluded—4x Tbolt weak and passive into stall.
decisions.notebook: G2 bring: Gengar-Mega+Gyarados lead, Mamoswine+Toxapex back. Plan: Mega Evo Gengar T1 for Shadow Tag, trap Rotom-W or Spiritomb. Gyarados Intimidate+Taunt to disrupt stall/Protect spam. Keep Mamoswine unburned—avoid Spiritomb WoW. Toxapex Haze resets Floette Calm Mind; Toxic wins attrition. Never expose Gyarados to Rotom-W Tbolt. If opponent leads Talonflame+Spiritomb, expect priority BB+Sucker Punch; Protect Gengar to scout, Ice Shard from back for Talonflame. Garchomp LifeOrb RoughSkin—Mamoswine Ice Shard KO range but RoughSkin chips back. Aegislash WideGuard blocks spread moves; target it with Shadow Ball from Gengar-Mega. Floette-Eternal Floettite unMega'd base 74 SpA—Calm Mind setup is the main wincon to watch; Haze/pressure it immediately.

Sucker Punch at -1 still deals 50-121% to Gengar with +1 priority, hitting before any Gengar attack. Spiritomb survives Mega Gengar Shadow Ball (44-53%). Rotom barely fears Gyarados (17-34%). Aggressive double-attack maximizes early pressure.

Mamoswine back has Focus Sash—immune to Tbolt but 4x weak to Hydro Pump. Floette-Eternal Calm Mind is opponent's main wincon; Toxapex Haze in back for that. Aegislash WideGuard blocks spread; target with Shadow Ball.

decisions.rationale: Sucker Punch min roll 43% guarantees KO on Gengar at 24% (priority beats Gengar's speed). Thunderbolt 4x OHKOs Gyarados through Sitrus (103-228%). Splitting targets pressures both; even if Gengar Protects, Gyarados likely dies (reduced Protect rate). Rotom survives any Gengar hit (max 49%).

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and the series 2-0 because the preview plan centered on Rotom-Wash as the preserved answer to Gengar and Gyarados, while Talonflame and Spiritomb handled Mamoswine, shut down Toxapex, and scouted Protect. Clean execution and the between-game emphasis on keeping Rotom healthy and using Protect/Taunt rather than forcing Hydro Pump helped rather than backfired. The four brought were correct: Talonflame, Spiritomb, Rotom-Wash, and Garchomp covered the actual opponent lineup, and evolving no Mega was fine because the non-Mega plan already worked; Mega Floette and Aegislash were low-value in this game. Prep was mostly right to register Rotom, Talonflame, Spiritomb, and Garchomp, but Mega Floette/Aegislash were not ideal, and Manectric could have been a more direct Electric-pressure option from the left-behind group.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, keep Rotom as the primary Gengar/Gyarados check and use Protect to bait Focus Sash, Intimidate, and Protect. Prefer Thunderbolt over risky Hydro Pump unless a Water KO is required. Use Spiritomb or Taunt to neutralize Toxapex, and never switch Garchomp into live Mamoswine. Treat Talonflame as Mamoswine/Gyarados pressure, not a Gengar switch-in. In future prep, consider Manectric or another Ghost-resistant Electric threat over Mega Floette/Aegislash, and keep Earthquake/Rock Slide ready for Corviknight.
reflections.notebook: Dark resists Ghost 0.5x here. Opponent leans on Protect-heavy Gengar, Focus Sash Mamoswine, Intimidate Gyarados, and status-only Toxapex. Toxapex is vulnerable to Taunt and Thunderbolt; Sucker Punch is not the answer to it. Rotom is the best durable check to Gengar and Gyarados if kept healthy and protected from Ground. Talonflame handles Mamoswine and Gyarados but must not be left to take Gengar Thunderbolt. Garchomp should be preserved for Corviknight and late-game Ground pressure, never switched into live Mamoswine. Expect Corviknight Tailwind/Brave Bird and Klefki Thunder Wave/Reflect in rematches; bring Rock Slide and Taunt/status-control answers. Prep conclusion: prioritize Rotom, Talonflame, Spiritomb, and Garchomp; Manectric is worth considering over Mega Floette or Aegislash for cleaner Electric pressure.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2. In game 2, the four brought (Gengar, Mamoswine, Gyarados, Toxapex) had fatal structural flaws: two Pokémon (Toxapex, Gyarados) were weak to Rotom-Wash's STAB Thunderbolt, and nothing reliably answered Talonflame's Gale Wings Brave Bird priority. Gengar entered at 24% HP (damaged in turns 1–3) making it nearly useless despite outspeeding the backline. The opponent consistently predicted Protect patterns, landing Brave Bird through predicted protects or double-targeting the non-protecting slot. Mamoswine's Sash was consumed early and it fell to Brave Bird. Corviknight and Klefki were left on the bench despite Corviknight resisting Brave Bird and checking Garchomp, and Klefki offering screens/Thunder Wave to slow the opponent's offensive pressure. Mega Gengar was a poor choice here: Shadow Tag doesn't trap Spiritomb (Ghost-type immunity), and Gengar's frailty meant it couldn't survive long enough to trap anything meaningful.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Corviknight over Toxapex or Gyarados — it resists Talonflame's Brave Bird and Garchomp's Rock Slide while providing Tailwind or Defog support. Consider Klefki for screens to buffer Gengar's frailty and Thunder Wave to neutralize Gale Wings speed. Avoid bringing two Electric-weak Pokémon against a Rotom-Wash team. Vary Protect timing — the opponent read Protect patterns cleanly across both games. If Mega Gengar is brought, it needs screen support or a safe switch-in path; entering at 24% made it dead weight. Greninja (left behind entirely) could have outspeed and threatened Floette/Garchomp with Ice Beam and Shadow Ball, potentially worth registering over Toxapex.

Opponent tendencies: leads Rotom-Wash + Spiritomb; backline Talonflame/Floette-Eternal/Garchomp/Aegislash. Predicts Protect patterns accurately and double-targets the unprotected slot. Relies on priority (Gale Wings Brave Bird, Sucker Punch) to pick off weakened targets.

Rotom-W Modest Levitate Sitrus (Thunderbolt/Hydro Pump/WoW/Protect). Floette-E Modest Floettite FlowerVeil (Moonblast/Psychic/Calm Mind/Protect). Garchomp Adamant LifeOrb RoughSkin (EQ/Rock Slide/Dragon Claw/Protect). Aegislash Modest SpellTag StanceChange (Shadow Ball/Flash Cannon/King's Shield/Wide Guard).

Prep conclusions: This opponent punishes predictable Protect usage and Electric-weak teams. Corviknight is the premier Talonflame answer and also checks Garchomp — strongly consider bringing it. Klefki screens help Gengar survive and Thunder Wave cripples Talonflame. Greninja's speed tier and coverage (Ice Beam for Garchomp, Shadow Ball for Aegislash) may be worth registering over Toxapex, who is too passive and Electric-weak here. Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag is partially nullified by Spiritomb's Ghost typing; weigh whether Gengar's speed is worth the frailty without screen support. Opponent's Floette-Eternal with Calm Mind + Flower Veil is a late-game sweeper threat if not addressed early.
